clue.text: Large chap backing female — as female

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the large chap's letters are read from right to left

parts.note: large means fat
Sid is a stock name for a chap

explanation.surface: A big man supports a woman, described as female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the large chap to give DISTAF. The first 'female' is wordplay; the second, after 'as', is the definition, a deliberate echo by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the maternal line, so the word serves as an adjective for things female.

clue.text: Engagement ring ripped from rampant toad, marriage's ending?

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
ripped from tells us one piece is torn out of the word that follows

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word marriage

explanation.surface: An engagement ring torn from a wild toad: is this the end of a marriage?
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from TOAD leaves TAD, which 'rampant' rearranges to DAT; add E from 'marriage's ending'.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is an appointment or engagement to meet someone.

clue.text: See 3
Letters mixed up in this anagram of "Paul has to be the foremost of pillocks!"

indicators.note: the clue openly calls the following words an anagram, so their letters are rearranged
the foremost of picks just the opening letter of the word pillocks

explanation.surface: The setter Paul jokes that he is the chief of the idiots, inside an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: PAUL HAS TO BE plus P from 'the foremost of pillocks' give twelve letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This soup contains pasta shapes of the alphabet floating about, so it is literally a jumble of letters.

clue.text: Raid Scrabble tiles J, A, Z, Z, I, L — what wouldn't one give ___ ?

definitions.meaning: a raid is a sudden attack or sally

definitions.text: Scrabble tiles J, A, Z, Z, I, L — what wouldn't one give ___ ?
definitions.meaning: with those tiles a player would give anything for the letter Y to spell a high-scoring word, so the blank reads as three words

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player with a rack full of high-value letters longs for one more tile.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled by three words, the second reading: J, A, Z, Z, I, L plus Y spells JAZZILY.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden raid or incursion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Thingummy making parties from the left and right sigh

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: from the right means reading the second party backwards, after the first read from the left

parts.note: the same word party, do, used a second time
ah is a sigh

explanation.surface: Something unnamed makes revellers on both sides sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties from the left and right' gives DO read forwards and DO read from the right, OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal placeholder words for an object whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Old star not widely accepted as deity

indicators.note: not tells us a piece is left out of the star

parts.note: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky
U means upper-class, hence socially accepted, a crossword convention

explanation.surface: A former star who never gained universal approval as a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the U, which stands for upper-class and so socially acceptable, from the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Single European into poet, his artistic interest superficial?

indicators.note: into means going inside the poet's name

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
I, the Roman numeral, is one or single
a Lett is a Latvian, a European

explanation.surface: A lone European enters a poet's life, whose interest in art is shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler in the arts whose interest is shallow rather than serious.

clue.text: Dutch in Rhodes (or abroad)

indicators.note: abroad suggests scattered far and wide, so the letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: A Dutch person in Rhodes, or perhaps somewhere else abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like a nationality, but in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is a man's wife. HER INDOORS is the jokey British term for a wife, from the TV series Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British terms a man uses for his wife.

clue.text: Attempt to pinch bottom (Widdecombe's bottom), worthless stuff

indicators.note: to pinch is to grab and hold, so the attempt closes round the rest

parts.note: try means attempt
the rump is the bottom

indicators.note: bottom here picks out the final letter of Widdecombe

explanation.surface: Someone tries to grope Ann Widdecombe, the prim British Conservative politician: utter rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY holds RUMP plus E, the last letter of Widdecombe.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery means showy but worthless things, nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Marilyn's husband, he with a literary tale?

definitions.meaning: the playwright Arthur ... was married to Marilyn Monroe
one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims tells a bawdy tale named after his grinding trade

explanation.surface: Monroe's spouse was a man with a famous story to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller wed Monroe, and the Canterbury Tales include one told by a grinder of corn.

clue.text: One opens gold sweet

parts.note: a gate is something that opens
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone opens a golden sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich cream cake, served as a sweet or dessert course.

clue.text: Nelson's ultimate ally, hot maid misbehaving?

definitions.text: Nelson's ultimate ally, hot maid misbehaving?

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so the letters are put out of order
ultimate picks the final letter of Nelson

explanation.surface: The admiral's last companion was a passionate servant girl behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: N (Nelson's ultimate) plus ALLY, HOT, MAID are rearranged; the whole clue also describes Emma Hamilton, Nelson's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Hamilton was Admiral Nelson's mistress, his companion until his death at Trafalgar.

clue.text: Hosiery primarily confiscated by officer in dissolute cabinet

indicators.note: something confiscated by an officer is taken into his hands, so it goes inside
dissolute means loose, so the letters of officer in are loosened
primarily takes the first letter of hosiery

explanation.surface: Stockings are seized by a debauched officer from a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissolute' signals the anagram, and 'confiscated by' puts the hosiery initial into it; 'cabinet' looks like government but is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiffonier is a tall chest of drawers or low sideboard, a kind of cabinet.

clue.text: Cash here in place of order for butterfly

indicators.note: in places the cash drawer inside the religious house

parts.note: a friary is where a religious order lives
cash is kept in a till

explanation.surface: Put money here instead of ordering a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' looks like 'instead of', but splits as 'in' plus 'place of order'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fritillary is a butterfly with chequered orange and black wings.

clue.text: Farrier starts to ride stallions, every steed wrapped by Father Christmas, perhaps?

indicators.note: wrapped by means enclosed, so the initials sit inside

parts.note: Santa is famous for laughing ho ho, so he is jokingly one who says it

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Santa wraps up each horse a blacksmith attends to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped by' puts the initials into Santa's laugh-word after its first two letters: Father Christmas, famous for 'ho ho', is a ho-ho-er, one who says it.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier is the craftsman who fits iron shoes to horses' hooves.

clue.text: Weed obscuring duck, work to see bird

indicators.note: obscuring means covering, so the garden tool's letters go around the rest

parts.note: to hoe is to weed
a duck in cricket is zero, O
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Weeds hiding a duck; work to spot a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with a long curved bill.

clue.text: Back a turn

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Return, a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in the past, as in some years back.

clue.text: Love: it comes up in county as loyalty

indicators.note: in places the love and the reversed word within the county

parts.note: Devon is a county of south-west England
love in tennis scores is zero, O

indicators.note: comes up means rising, which in a down clue is reading backwards

explanation.surface: Love arises in a county as faithfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns the word 'it' to TI, since in a down clue rising means reading backwards; 'in' places it with the love inside the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion means loyal and faithful commitment.

clue.text: Well, the answer should __ here

definitions.meaning: the solver's entry should slot into these three squares

explanation.surface: A setter's aside that the solution should go in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit means in good health, and an answer fits its space.

clue.text: One drugged in myth, some years on consuming flower to save time

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the rest goes inside

parts.note: later means some years on

indicators.note: to save means to keep in hand, so the river holds the time letter

parts.note: a flower is a river, something that flows: here the Ouse, a river in England

explanation.surface: Some years later someone eats a flower to save time.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is a river, something that flows; 'to save' puts the time inside it, and 'consuming' puts the result inside the years-on word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey the lotus-eaters ate a narcotic plant and lost all wish to go home.

clue.text: You overlooking partners? Past it and still on the shelf?

indicators.note: overlooking means sitting above, so in a down answer these come first

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
N and S, North and South, are partners in bridge
past it means old

explanation.surface: You ignore your partners: are you old and left on the shelf?
explanation.definitionFit: Unsold goods remain on the shop shelf because no one has bought them.

clue.text: Actor offering setter flower

parts.note: Orlando is a pseudonymous Guardian crossword setter
a bloom is a flower

explanation.surface: An actor offering the crossword compiler a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Bloom is an English actor, known from The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Bulb may be wasted

definitions.meaning: a light bulb may be switched on and shining

explanation.surface: The bulb may have been a waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp can be illuminated, and lit up is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Biblical character among people, a harlot

indicators.note: among tells us the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A biblical figure among the crowd, a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Leah was Jacob's first wife in Genesis.

clue.text: Mix porridge here

definitions.meaning: porridge is British slang for a prison term, served in jail

explanation.surface: Instructions to mix the oats here.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge, British slang for time inside, is served in stir, slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir means mix, and it is also slang for the prison where one serves time.

clue.text: Running, I did so backwards — ouch!

indicators.note: backwards means the past tense of running is written in reverse

parts.note: did so refers back to running, so it is ran
ow is a cry like ouch

explanation.surface: Someone out running went backwards and hurt themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did so' stands for 'ran'; reversed it gives NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In a row means consecutively, one after another, as in a running streak.

clue.text: Filth repulsed in broadcast, commanding attention

indicators.note: in places the reversed filth inside

parts.note: to broadcast is to send out, so sent

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dirt is filth

explanation.surface: Disgusting content was rejected on air because it demanded notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns the filth round to TRID, and 'in' puts that inside the broadcast word.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and harsh, forcing people to take notice.

clue.text: Hardy novel about capital of Ireland — or of somewhere else?

definitions.text: Hardy novel about capital of Ireland — or of somewhere else?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement
capital of picks the first letter of Ireland

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy novel set in Dublin, or some other city?
explanation.walkthrough: HARDY plus I are rearranged; the result is the capital of somewhere other than Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia, somewhere far from Ireland.

clue.text: Hot dog filled with hot cat?

indicators.note: filled with means another piece is stuffed inside

parts.note: a hot dog pants, so jokingly it is a panter
H is short for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A frankfurter stuffed with something spicy: a hot cat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' looks like the sausage but is a panting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard or a puma.
